text.p: These are the headlines for selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Paul Martin plays it safe on budget: More than C$1-billion to be spent on jobs, social areas; deficit reaches 15-year low.
- Grits can't kick the deficit habit: With an election coming, voters won't be allowed to change focus.
- Brigade plan links NATO, Russia: U.S. proposal aims to allay fears.
- Vancouver police target sex customers: Prosecuting the prostitutes has not worked in drive against vice in the streets.
- Revved-up house market puts agents in overdrive: Pent-up demand helps fuel current boom, executive says.
- Gulf wins bid for Clyde: Canadian company gains control of prized North Sea oil assets in C$1.11-billion takeover.
- Investors wallop Bre-X stock: Indonesian alleges Busang deal illegal.
- Minivans losing their appeal: Demographics may be behind sales slip.
- CN concedes defeat in bid for CP Rail's eastern lines.
- An unusual team, on paper: The two bosses of newly created Abitibi-Consolidated bring diverse operating styles to an unlikely power-sharing setup.
- Martin adjusts fiscal course on way to election call: 'We see that the worst is behind us...the era of cuts is ending.'
